title: Unify analytics observability: journey-based SLIs, tracing anchors, and dashboard templates
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Our analytics ingestion and console backend produce multi-tenant telemetry used by billing, product analytics, and the Console dashboards. Currently teams define SLIs and dashboards ad-hoc per feature which causes alert fatigue, inconsistent coverage across critical customer journeys, and long mean-time-to-detect for regressions.

Goal: Deliver a unified observability baseline for analytics services focused on "journey"-level SLIs (end-to-end user flows), a small set of tracing "anchors" to quickly root-cause high-latency paths, and templated dashboards and alerts that can be applied to new pipelines. This will reduce detection time for degradations, standardize severity/response, and simplify onboarding of new analytics components.

Success metrics: 
- Mean detection time for analytic ingestion regressions reduced >= 40% within two months of rollout.
- Number of duplicate/overlapping alerts across analytics reduced by >= 60%.
- >= 90% of new analytics pipelines onboarded to templates within their first deployment.

Scope: 
- Define 5 journey-based SLIs (ingest latency, batch-to-query freshness, per-tenant event loss, storage write error rate, end-to-end dashboard render latency).
- Instrument tracing anchors at: API ingress, router/sampler, batch queue, transform worker, object-store write, and query layer join.
- Create 3 dashboard templates: Operational (SLIs & KPIs), Investigation (trace waterfall + debug logs), and Capacity (throughput & KV-cache hit/miss).
- Provide templated alert rules and runbook playbooks (triage checklist, mitigation steps, rollback links).

Non-goals: Detailed per-feature UX dashboards, rearchitecting the ingestion pipeline, or changing billing metrics. Those will be handled separately.

Approach: 
1) Define canonical journeys and map them to existing traces and metrics. Reuse existing SLI definitions where possible (e.g., per-tenant availability from ENG-61234).
2) Implement lightweight tracing anchors (Span tags + consistent trace ids) in analytics gateway and transform workers; propagate trace context through batch boundaries.
3) Add SLI calculations in analytics metrics service with labels for journey and tenant. Create SLI exporters for the SLO service.
4) Build Grafana dashboard templates (JSON) and Console-integrated panels for the Console UI.
5) Draft runbooks and embed links to GitHub PRs and incidentplaybooks.

Deliverables: 
- Spec doc: "Journey SLI catalog and tracing anchor spec" (Confluence link in links).
- Implementation PRs: gateway, worker, metrics-service changes.
- Grafana JSON templates and Console panels.
- Runbook + PagerDuty escalation map.

Rollout plan: 
- Week 1: Spec review & approvals (PM, Reliability, Security).
- Week 2-3: Instrumentation PRs for gateway + transform workers behind feature flag.
- Week 4: Metrics exporters and dashboard templates.
- Week 5: Canary onboard 2 non-critical tenants, evaluate alerts, iterate.
- Week 6: Full rollout and doc handoff to SRE/Oncall.

Risks & mitigation: 
- High cardinality metrics from per-tenant labels — mitigate with histogram bucketing and cardinality limits; use aggregated SLI computations where appropriate.
- Trace propagation across batch windows may be lossy — use anchor spans with batch-id tagging to correlate traces to batches.
- Alert noise during rollout — start with detection-level alerts (P3) and escalate thresholds after 2 canaries.

Operational notes: 
- Default SLO targets proposed: 99.5% ingest success over 30d for production tenants, 95th percentile ingest-to-query < 6s for streaming pipelines, 99% dashboard render < 2s. These are proposals and must be validated with PM and SRE.
- Suggested alert thresholds: SLI burn rate > 2x for 15m (P1), sustained SLO breach over 1h (P0).

Required approvals: PM (Maya Chen), SRE lead (Jon Kim), Security (Nina Orlov).
